RagShortTexts: The ruling elite of Kartli comprised ancient aristocratic houses and military dynasties competing for feudal land and fiscal control.
Domestic politics were profoundly steered by court intrigues and noble factions resisting excessive central centralization.
Intricate matrimonial alliances and blood feuds permeated the nobility, ensuring that disputed successions frequently sparked nationwide crises.

Variants.Content: Within the opulent halls and sprawling feudal estates of Kartli, the balance of domestic power remained in perilous equilibrium. Ancient lineages commanded vast agricultural latifundia, hereditary warrior retinues, and lucrative trade monopolies, acting simultaneously as imperial cornerstones and covert rivals to the throne. Court assemblies seethed with venomous factionalism, pitting entrenched senatorial aristocrats against battle-hardened military commanders who demanded greater political dominance. Behind tapestried corridors, clandestine poisonings, forged wills, and intercepted treaties dictated political ascendancy. Lesser vassals maneuvered cautiously between dominant magnates, ready to shift allegiance whenever the central authority showed signs of exhaustion or military defeat.

Two noble houses clash in the market square of the royal town, and the royal guards push the crowd back with their shields. The feud began over a vineyard boundary, and blood is spilled before the magistrates arrive. A common spearman takes a cut meant for a lord's nephew, and his name is entered in no ledger.

Speaking to his heir, the lord says the crown is only as strong as the families who swear to it. Keep your vineyards and fortress walls in good repair, he says, and never let a rival marry a daughter of your house. At court, bow to the king's chosen ministers, but send your own man to watch the mountain passes.
